AN.title: make A2 decidable while the log is being written

AN.note:
MEASURED 24 Aug 2026. A2 is not failing because replay is broken -- replay reproduces exactly. It fails because `doctor` compares the persisted projection against a replay of the *live* log, and with ~20 agents appending, events land between the two reads. Observed in one sitting, same repository, minutes apart: FAIL ('canonical state diverged'), then UNKNOWN ('state covers N of M events'), then PASS -- the last only because the rebuild and the check happened in the same instant.

So the condition as written is decidable only on a quiet repository, and this repository is never quiet. A gate that reports three different verdicts for one unchanged history is measuring contention, not replay.

Fix it by deciding A2 against a **pinned prefix**: take the projection's own high-water mark, replay exactly that many events, and compare. Events appended after the mark are outside the comparison -- they are not evidence of divergence and must not be reported as such. A genuine mismatch inside the prefix must still FAIL, and an empty prefix must still be UNKNOWN (do not reintroduce the tautological pass repaired on 20 Aug 2026).

The test is the point of this unit: `tests/test_doctor_a2_concurrent.py` must append to the log *while* the check runs and assert the verdict is stable and correct. A test that only runs on a quiet log reproduces the bug it is meant to catch.

Do NOT make A2 pass by widening what counts as identical. The divergence report is right in principle; the read window is what is wrong.

AU.title: narrow the cursor lock to startup so Cursor capacity is usable

AU.note:
MEASURED 24 August 2026. The principal reports Cursor quota at 4% used while Claude and Codex are saturated, and this is why.

`scripts/dispatch.py` wraps the ENTIRE cursor-composer run in ExclusiveFileLock(DEFAULT_CURSOR_LOCK) for the full leash. With a 3600s leash that means one cursor dispatch per hour: extras block their whole leash and then fail with 'cursor-agent lock held'. Three units burned an hour each that way on 24 Aug, and build_driver.py had to add CURSOR_CONCURRENCY = 1 to stop the driver wasting slots on dispatches that could never start.

WHAT THE LOCK PROTECTS, measured: the comment says two cursor-agent processes race `~/.cursor/cli-config.json`. That file contains NO credentials -- only preferences (approvalMode, display, permissions, sandbox, version). Its mtime on 24 Aug was 21 Aug 22:24, THREE DAYS STALE, across dozens of cursor dispatches. So ordinary runs do not write it at all; it is written only when a setting changes.

So the lock's EXISTENCE is defensible and its SCOPE is not: an hour-long exclusive hold protects a file written perhaps weekly, and it costs almost all of a paid quota.

Narrow it to the window where contention is real -- process startup, when the config is read -- and release it once the child is running. Measure where the write actually happens before choosing the boundary; do not guess the number. If cursor-agent turns out to write the config on exit too, say so and cover both ends rather than pretending one is enough.

Then raise CURSOR_CONCURRENCY in .harness/build_driver.py to match what the narrowed lock genuinely allows, and say what you measured it to be.

DO NOT simply delete the lock. A corrupted cli-config.json would break every cursor dispatch at once, and the race is real even if rare. The test must prove two concurrent dispatches can run AND that the config survives them intact.

AV.title: read the cross-family verdict instead of discarding it
AV.commit: fix(driver): consume the review verdict and block retirement on a bad one
AV.note:
MEASURED 24 August 2026, and this is the most beta-adverse defect in the build.

The driver dispatches a cross-family review for every built unit -- a DIFFERENT MODEL FAMILY from the builder, which is the only genuinely different class of evidence in the whole pipeline -- writes the reviewer's output to `<uid>-verify.out`, and then NEVER READS IT. `state["verified"]` is read at build_driver.py:1138 and :1142 and initialised at :1082, and NOTHING WRITES A UNIT INTO IT. The 19 entries currently there came from a hand-run review on 23 Aug, not from the pipeline.

So every review is dispatched, billed against the principal's quota, and discarded. The system performs consilience and throws away the result. Per CONSILIENCE.md the whole project rests on convergence from a different class of facts being a TEST -- a test whose outcome is never read is not a test, and a unit marked done on the builder's say-so alone is exactly the echo this repository exists to refuse.

What to build: parse `<uid>-verify.out` for a structured verdict, record it in `state["verified"]` and in the TRAJECTORY, and make a unit's retirement depend on it. A SOUND verdict retires the unit. A verdict finding blocking defects must PREVENT retirement and put the unit back for repair with the findings attached.

Require the reviewer to emit a machine-readable verdict; do not regex prose for the word 'sound'. An unparseable verdict is NOT a pass -- fail closed, because the whole point is that the absence of evidence stopped being treated as evidence.

Evidence for how strict this should be: the one hand-run cross-family review of 19 units found 0 sound, 5 blocking and 68 surviving findings, and 14 of 19 carried a guard that could be deleted with the suite still green. Reviewed is not sound, and the pipeline currently cannot tell the difference.

Do NOT make the verdict advisory-only to keep throughput up. Throughput through an unmeasured filter is the thing being sold here, and it is worth less than nothing.

PRIORITY 25, set deliberately on 24 August 2026. This unit unblocks nothing, so ordering by downstream impact would dispatch it last. That is backwards: it does not release work, it makes every unit already released trustworthy. Until it lands, 'done' means one model said so.

AR.title: narrow the held-out refusal to brief, worktree and claims, and void a measurement on contract leakage
AR.commit: fix(gate): refuse a held-out contract reachable from brief, worktree or claims
AR.note:
GATE WORK for A1 — ". Specified by the gate-diagnosis workflow on 24 August 2026 after reading the code; every claim in this brief was measured, not assumed.

Read ADR-0103's Enforcement section before touching anything. This unit REPAIRS K01 (commit 46e08ae), it does not undo it.

THE DEFECT, measured 24 August 2026. `.github/scripts/check_heldout_isolation.py` is 24 lines and refuses UNCONDITIONALLY: `refusal_reason()` returns a refusal for any argument and `main()` always returns 2. `scripts/dispatch.py:2500-2508` refuses any `--heldout-contract` before preflight, and its help text at dispatch.py:2458-2460 says 'refused until dispatch gains real isolation'. The consequence is that no held-out contract can be supplied to any dispatch on this architecture, so no contract-beta can be measured, so EXP-142 stays BLOCKED on its precondition and units K02, K03, K04 and AS all have nothing to stand on.

WHY THIS IS A REPAIR AND NOT A RELAXATION, and you must be able to state this yourself before you write a line. ADR-0103's Enforcement specifies the boundary exactly: 'refuses a build dispatch whose brief, worktree or claims can reach the held-out contract for that unit.' K01 refused on a broader ground -- that a same-OS-user unsandboxed child can read any file in principle -- which is true, and which converted the principal's guard into a wall that blocks his own decision. Narrowing to the specified boundary is implementing the decision. It is a relaxation ONLY if you leave the residual open, which is why the second half of this unit is mandatory and not optional.

WHAT TO BUILD.
(a) Make `check_heldout_isolation.py` decide rather than assert. It takes the contract path and the dispatch's brief text, worktree root and declared claims, and refuses when the contract is inside the worktree, named or quoted in the brief, or covered by any claim. It PERMITS otherwise, and prints what it checked. `scripts/dispatch.py` calls it with the real values instead of refusing on the flag's mere presence.
(b) Add a post-build audit mode to the SAME file -- do not create a second script. It reads the child's transcript (`<uid>.out`, `<uid>.err` under `.harness/dispatch/`) and the produced diff, and reports LEAKED if the contract's path, its sha256, or any of its distinctive content lines appear. A leaked measurement is VOID, not merely flagged.
(c) For (b), REUSE `.github/scripts/check_private_corpus.py`'s existing whole-line shingle fingerprinting -- case-folded words, >=12 words and >=80 characters, SHA-256 digests. Do not write a new fingerprinter. This is already in the codebase and it is the same problem.

WHAT YOU MUST NOT DO. Do not delete the refusal path -- a contract inside the worktree must still be refused before child launch, and `tests/test_heldout_isolation.py::test_heldout_contract_refuses_before_dispatch_preflight` must keep passing in substance. Do not build a container, a second OS user or a WSL uid boundary; that is weeks of Windows work for a residual (b) already covers, and nothing here has been measured to support it. Do not print the contract's contents in any refusal or audit output -- follow `check_private_corpus.py`, which never prints a matched private path in full.

RECORD THE RESIDUAL HONESTLY, in the module docstring: a child that reads the contract and neither echoes its path nor reproduces its assertions is not detected. Tag it `[asserted]`. That sentence is load-bearing for EXP-142's write-up and must not be softened.

DONE WHEN: a dispatch whose worktree, brief or claims can reach the contract is refused with exit 2 before child launch; a dispatch that cannot reach it proceeds; the audit mode returns LEAKED on a transcript containing the contract path, its digest, or a fingerprinted line, and CLEAN otherwise; every assertion above has a test that fails if the behaviour is removed.

AX.title: author a different-family held-out contract from pre-registered intent and commit its digest before dispatch
AX.commit: feat(gate): author a held-out contract from a different family before the build
AX.note:
GATE WORK for A1 — ". Specified by the gate-diagnosis workflow on 24 August 2026 after reading the code; every claim in this brief was measured, not assumed.

This is K02, re-specified against the narrowed K01. It cannot run until unit 1 lands, because dispatch refuses every held-out contract until then.

WHAT MUST EXIST, per ADR-0103's Decision section. The contract is derived from the SAME stated intent as the build, by a DIFFERENT model family from the builder, committed before the build dispatch, and never placed anywhere the builder or its checks can read.

CONCRETELY.
(a) The intent statement is the unit's `title` and `note` from `.harness/plan-units.json`. That is what already exists and it is pre-registered by construction -- do not invent a new intent format.
(b) Author the contract by dispatching to a family different from the one that will build, using the family selection machinery already in `scripts/dispatch.py`. The family difference must be REFUSED AT DISPATCH if violated, not merely logged. ADR-0103 names this as one of its three checks.
(c) Write the contract OUTSIDE the unit worktree and outside anything the claims cover, so unit 1's reachability check passes.
(d) Append a `measurement.registered` trajectory event with `config_hash` = the sha256 of the contract file, BEFORE the build dispatch starts. `src/consilient/events.py:286-336` already validates this event kind and requires 64 lower-case hex; `.github/scripts/check_measurement_recorded.py` already proves CI refuses a result without prior registration. Reuse both. Do not invent a new event kind and do not write the digest into a JSON side-file.

WHY THE DIGEST MATTERS MORE THAN IT LOOKS. The commitment is what stops the contract being rewritten after the artefact exists to match what the builder did -- Goodhart through the front door, which ADR-0103 names as the thing that would make beta_T measure nothing. Without a pre-committed digest, 'authored before the build' is a claim nobody can check afterwards.

WHAT YOU MUST NOT DO. Do not let the caller supply the family of either side -- derive the builder's family from the dispatch that will actually run. Do not weaken the refusal in unit 1 to make placement convenient; move the file instead. Do not have the contract-authoring dispatch see the artefact, the builder's brief beyond the intent text, or the repository's own test suite for the claimed paths.

WATCH FOR THE TRIPWIRE, and record it: a contract that never marks a violation is not evidence of quality, it is evidence the contract was written to match what the builder was going to do anyway. The violation rate must be recorded alongside every contract so EXP-142 can report it.

DONE WHEN: a build dispatch for a measured unit refuses unless a contract digest is already in the trajectory and the authoring family differs from the builder's; the contract file sits outside the worktree and outside the claims; and a test fails if either refusal is removed.

AY.title: admit contract_beta as a gate estimand, strictly separate from human-beta and from every proxy
AY.commit: feat(beta): admit contract-beta for the gate, refusing every proxy estimand
AY.note:
GATE WORK for A1 — ". Specified by the gate-diagnosis workflow on 24 August 2026 after reading the code; every claim in this brief was measured, not assumed.

This is K03, re-specified. It deps on AT only because AT already claims `src/consilient/projection.py` and claims are locks -- there is no logical dependency between signed verdicts and contract-beta, and the two code regions do not overlap.

WHAT EXISTS TODAY, measured 24 August 2026. `src/consilient/beta.py:39-47` defines `HUMAN_VERDICT_BETA = 'human_verdict_beta'` and `PROXY_ESTIMAND_KINDS = {mutation_proxy_beta, critic_proxy_beta, repository_consequence_false_shipment_cohort_lower_bound}`. `admits_human_beta_row` (beta.py:183-191) refuses every proxy and requires `auth_status == 'authenticated'`. `projection.py:66-67, 979, 1030-1034, 1141-1145` writes `estimand_kind` and `auth_status` onto outcome rows, and hardcodes `'human_verdict_beta'` at both write sites. Nothing anywhere writes or reads a contract-beta row. Grep for `contract_beta` across src, tests, docs, scripts and .github returns only ADR-0103 and EXP-142 prose.

WHAT TO BUILD.
(a) A `CONTRACT_BETA = 'contract_beta'` estimand kind and an `admits_gate_row()` that admits it and NOTHING else. It must refuse every kind in `PROXY_ESTIMAND_KINDS`, refuse `human_verdict_beta`, and refuse any row whose `auth_status` is not authenticated.
(b) `admits_human_beta_row` must be left EXACTLY as it is. The two admission rules stay separate functions with separate tests. ADR-0103 is explicit: human-beta is alignment, reported separately, never blocking, and its rule is 'unchanged and continues to refuse every proxy'.
(c) A projection write path that records a contract-beta outcome row: the held-out contract's verdict (violation or not) as the condition, and the project's own checks' verdict (accept or reject) as the outcome. beta_T = P(checks accept | contract violated). The row must carry the repository it was measured on, because A1 reports per repository and pooling is forbidden.
(d) A row whose measurement was marked LEAKED by unit 1's audit must be REFUSED here, not silently included.

WHAT YOU MUST NOT DO, and this is the whole point of the separation. Do not widen `PROXY_ESTIMAND_KINDS` and do not admit anything in it into the gate projection. `critic_proxy_beta`, `mutation_proxy_beta` and the repository-consequence lower bound are DIFFERENT ESTIMANDS, not cheaper estimates of the same one -- ADR-0080's algebra is that they 'say nothing about H without labels'. Do not perform the substitution `q_upper := beta_upper` that ADR-0080 forbids. Do not admit a `declared_principal` auth status: `scripts/verdict.py` lets its caller choose the principal, so a local agent process can forge one, and admitting it would let the system fabricate the ground truth used to measure its own error rate.

Do not lower `MIN_REJECTIONS` or add a knob that can lower a floor. beta.py:216-219 already refuses a `min_rejections` below the constant; contract-beta needs its own floor with the same property -- raisable only.

DONE WHEN: `admits_gate_row` admits a clean contract_beta row and refuses each of the four other kinds by name in a test; a leaked row is refused; `admits_human_beta_row`'s behaviour is byte-for-byte unchanged and a test proves it; and a Wilson interval is computed per repository with no pooling path available.

AZ.title: gate A1 on contract-beta over two repositories, read from the trajectory rather than a prose regex

AZ.note:
GATE WORK for A1 — ". Specified by the gate-diagnosis workflow on 24 August 2026 after reading the code; every claim in this brief was measured, not assumed.

This supersedes BOTH unit AS and unit K04, which are near-duplicates claiming `src/consilient/cli.py` for the same change on different dep chains. Retire whichever survives; do not run both.

THE DEFECT, measured 24 August 2026. `src/consilient/cli.py:426-484` computes A1 from one input: EXP-01's entry in `docs/10-research/experiment-register.md`. `EXP01_BETA` (cli.py:94-96) matches `beta-measured: p [lo, hi]`; cli.py:433-452 sets `stopping_rule_fired` from the literal string 'stopping rule FIRED' and hard-fails. ADR-0103 is the principal's own decision, dated 23 August 2026, and it moved the gate quantity to contract-beta (beta_T). The decision moved and the code did not follow. Implement his decision; do not invent one.

WHAT TO BUILD.
(a) A1 reads the contract-beta projection from the TRAJECTORY via `admits_gate_row`, not a regex over markdown. Delete the `EXP01_BETA` route from A1 entirely.
(b) A1 requires TWO repositories, each with its own interval, never pooled. (e) Human-beta is reported SEPARATELY and blocks nothing. ADR-0103's reasoning is the principal's own and must be preserved: he is by design a weaker judge of the system's output than the system, so a gate resting on his verdicts measures agreement with the weaker judge rather than correctness.

THE PROSE-EDIT HOLE, which you must close and not reproduce. `tests/test_v0_invariants.py:2871-2885` proves A1 currently reports PASS if someone edits the register to drop 'stopping rule FIRED' while keeping a `beta-measured:` line. Do not admit a proxy estimand; `PROXY_ESTIMAND_KINDS` exists precisely to keep `critic_proxy_beta`, `mutation_proxy_beta` and the repository-consequence lower bound out of the projection, and that separation stands. Do not make A1 depend on human-beta. Do not make it pass. ADR-0103's Enforcement section says in terms: 'none of these exists today ... Gate A1 must continue to report FAIL. That is stated here so nobody reads this ADR as having opened it.'

DONE WHEN: A1 reports FAIL with a reason naming the ABSENT contract-beta measurement rather than the retired EXP-01 route; a test fails if A1 ever passes without an interval; a test fails if A1 passes on a proxy estimand; a test fails if A1 passes on one repository; a test fails if A1 passes while ADR-0103 is PROVISIONAL; and no A1 code path reads `docs/10-research/experiment-register.md`.

BA.title: Make the canonical state digest independent of where the log lives
BA.commit: fix(projection): digest the log's content, not its absolute path
BA.note:
GATE WORK for A2 — R. Specified by the gate-diagnosis workflow on 24 August 2026 after reading the code; every claim in this brief was measured, not assumed.

THE DEFECT. Gate A2 fails deterministically on this repository, and the state does not diverge. `state_digest` (src/consilient/projection.py:1544) hashes every column of every table, and `rejections.path` (written by `_apply_rejections`, src/consilient/projection.py:279, insert at :291) holds the ABSOLUTE filesystem path of the file a refused line came from — `events.Rejection.path`, src/consilient/events.py:337, populated by `read_all` at :2852. Unit AN's pinned-prefix comparison (landed as 7e9bd0e) must rebuild the prefix in a scratch directory, `db.parent / (db.stem + "-a2-prefix")` at src/consilient/cli.py:321, so every rejection row it produces carries a different path from the persisted one. Any log with at least one refused line therefore reports 'canonical state diverged' forever. This one has six permanent ones (2026-08-20.jsonl lines 62/63/66 baselined by ADR-0043; 2026-08-22.jsonl lines 27/35/45).

THE EVIDENCE. [measured] 24 August 2026, on a frozen copy of `.harness/state.db` (2945 events) and `.harness/log`, reproducing `cmd_replay`'s comparison exactly: persisted digest `58da482c07c766…`, pinned-prefix digest `b6f2804443ef26…`. A per-table digest of both databases: every table identical EXCEPT `rejections`, 6 rows on each side, identical `id`, `line` and `reason` on all six, differing only in `path`. Rewrite `rejections.path` to its basename on both sides, re-digest, and both give `d9438ac950072222…`. A2 passes on this history the moment the path is normalised. Reproduce this before you change anything; if your reproduction disagrees, stop and report rather than proceeding.

WHAT TO DO. Two changes, both small.

1. Store the log-relative name, not the absolute path. In `_apply_rejections`, normalise the value written to `rejections.path` to the daily file's name (the log directory is flat — `read_all` and `_copy_event_prefix` both use `glob("*.jsonl")`). Do NOT change `Rejection.path` itself: it is returned out of `read_all` and used by the dashboard and by `cmd_replay`'s `quarantined` payload, where the full path is wanted. Normalise only at the database boundary. Nothing reads `rejections.path` back out of the database — verify that yourself before you rely on it.

2. Stamp the projection so the one-off change is not misreported as divergence. Adding (1) changes the digest, so the FIRST run after this lands would compare an old-code database against a new-code rebuild and report 'canonical state diverged' — a false failure on the very gate that exists to catch false verdicts, and the same false failure will recur on every future change to `SCHEMA`, `_apply` or `state_digest`. So: add a module constant `PROJECTION_VERSION` in projection.py, bump it in this commit, write it with `PRAGMA user_version = …` in `build` (sqlite has this built in — do NOT add a table; a new table would itself be covered by `state_digest`), read it from the existing database in `cmd_replay` before digesting, and when it differs from the code's constant have `_replay_condition` return status `unknown` with a reason naming both versions. This is the version half of unit AC, which is NOT in HEAD (`git merge-base --is-ancestor c91aa66 HEAD` fails); whoever lands AC later must merge with this rather than revert it.

WHAT MUST NOT BE DONE. Do not touch the prefix pinning — AN is correct and is the reason A2 is decidable at all while the log is being written. Do not widen what counts as identical, do not drop `rejections.path` from the digest (a rejection moving files must still change it), and do not make the version stamp an escape hatch: `PROJECTION_VERSION` is a constant in code, never derived from data or from the database being read, and a version MISMATCH yields `unknown`, never `pass`. A genuine mismatch inside the prefix under the SAME version must still FAIL. Do not reintroduce the tautological pass repaired on 20 August 2026: an empty prefix stays `unknown`. Do not touch `_object_status` (src/consilient/projection.py:1149) — its working-tree dependence is a real latent defect of the same shape, but it is measured NOT to be the cause here (prefix digests with `workspace=REPO` and `workspace=None` are both `b6f2804443ef26…`, and `record_facts` is empty) and it belongs to its own unit.

HOW YOU KNOW YOU ARE FINISHED. (a) tests/test_doctor_a2_concurrent.py gains a case that puts an UNREADABLE line in the log — this is the hole that let the defect through, since none of its five existing tests ever produces a rejection — and asserts A2 is `pass` with the prefix comparison intact. (b) A case asserting a same-version genuine divergence inside the prefix still returns `fail`, and (c) a case asserting a version mismatch returns `unknown`, not `pass` and not `fail`. (d) Run `consil doctor` in this worktree twice in succession: the first run may report A2 `unknown` for the version change, the second must report `pass` with a reason naming 2945-or-more compared events. Report the actual output of both runs; do not claim the gate moved without pasting what doctor said.

THE ADR MUST GET THE CAUSE RIGHT. Two claims in the earlier draft are false and must not be repeated. These three are INTERIOR, with valid lines after them and the file ending cleanly; AB would have caught none of them. BJ.title: decide whether a unit may merge into a red tree, and enforce the answer
BJ.commit: fix(driver): settle the merge-into-red policy and enforce it
BJ.note:
MEASURED 24 August 2026. `merge_unit_worktree` is called from the merge loop at build_driver.py:1453; `suite_green()` is not called until :1480. So units MERGE INTO THE TREE BEFORE the suite is consulted, and a red tree keeps accepting work.

An orphaned worktree (AI2, from 12:55 that day, never in the plan and never merged) had already found this and added a `suite_ok` parameter to refuse the merge. Its implementation is stale -- the driver has changed substantially since -- but the invariant it encodes is real, and its test `test_merge_refuses_red_tree` names it exactly.

THIS IS A POLICY DECISION AND YOU MUST ARGUE IT, not just implement fail-closed.

FOR refusing: merging into a red tree compounds breakage. The newly merged unit inherits a broken state it did not cause, its own verification is meaningless against that baseline, and isolating the original cause gets harder with every unit added on top. On 24 Aug the reviewers proved this concretely -- they ran the suite, found it red, reported that, and produced no verdict at all, so 44 reviews were spent for nothing.

AGAINST refusing, and this is why it is not obvious: it can DEADLOCK. If the tree is red and the fix lives in an unmerged unit, refusing every merge keeps it red for ever. That happened on 24 Aug -- the tree was red and the repair came from the orchestrator by hand, not from the queue. A gate that can only be opened by the thing it blocks is a wall.

So the answer is probably conditional rather than absolute: refuse the merge UNLESS the unit's own claims intersect the failing tests, or unless a named escape is recorded in the trajectory. Whatever you choose, the reasoning goes in the code where the next person reads it, and the escape is recorded rather than implicit.

Do NOT simply copy AI2's implementation. Read it (git -C .harness/unit-worktrees/AI2 show HEAD) for its reasoning and its tests, then decide against the CURRENT driver, which has since gained atomic state, force_done, critical-path ordering, duplicate-build detection and a unit-loss tripwire.

BK.title: merge acceptance gate: the two checks ruff and mypy do not have

BK.note:

THE DEFECT. A merged Python file can be silently wrong in ways no tool in this repository detects. Unit T01's blind union produced a file that PARSED CLEANLY and carried four defects; three were invisible to the parser. Two of those three are already covered by tools we own (see MRG2) and two are covered by nothing.

THE EVIDENCE [measured 24 Aug 2026, HEAD 71a8433, specimen and prototypes in the scratchpad at .../4119b9a5-e07e-43de-bc2f-e873fbd124d2/scratchpad/t01/]. A 30-line reproduction carrying (a) KINDS bound twice at module level with the second binding omitting STATE, (b) a CREATE TABLE cut mid-statement inside a SCHEMA string literal, (c) a call stranded after a return:

BL.note:
MERGE RESILIENCE. Specified by the merge-resolution workflow on 24 August 2026 after reading the code and measuring against the live tree. Every claim in this brief was measured.

THE DEFECT. Three separate faults in the same region of the driver, all measured live today at HEAD 71a8433.

  (1) The already-landed detector at .harness/build_driver.py:1449 greps commit SUBJECTS: `git log --format=%H --fixed-strings --grep <subject> HEAD`, and on any hit it retires the unit.   (2) state["conflicts"][uid] is written on merge failure and cleared only by the re-test loop, never by retirement. K01 is in state["force_done"] AND on the escalation banner simultaneously, right now [measured].

  (3) Nothing runs any check on the tree a cherry-pick produces. `ruff check .` (32 errors) and `mypy --strict src/consilient` (17 errors) are BOTH already wired into .github/workflows/invariants.yml at lines 39 and 36, both are RED on HEAD today, and their errors are the bad-merge signature: 17 no-redef in harness.py, a stray `from typing import cast` at the end of tests/test_recall_receipts.py, three duplicated test functions and two uses of an undefined LOCK in docs/10-research/experiments/exp43/test_exp43.py [measured]. The gate exists, is correct, and is read by nobody in the merge path.

WHAT TO BUILD, in merge_unit_worktree (line 843) and the conflict re-test loop (around 1440-1480).

  A. Replace the subject grep with CONTENT COVERAGE. For each added non-blank line of the unit's own commits (`git show --format= -U0 <sha>`), ask whether that line is present in HEAD's copy of the same file (`git show HEAD:<path>`). Retire as already-landed at >= 99% coverage AND at least 20 added lines; below either bar, fall through and stay escalated. Measured today this retires T02 (1335 added lines, 0 absent) and K01 (77 added, 1 absent) -- both of which patch-id AND the subject grep miss, because both landed by hand-merge under a rewritten subject.

  B. Keep `git cherry HEAD <worktree-head>` as a cheap first rung but NEVER let it retire alone. git patch-id normalises whitespace, and in Python whitespace is the language: a commit that moves a statement into a loop has the same patch-id as one that does not.   C. Pass --merge-base=<sha>^ to the staleness merge-tree call at line 1474. The driver predicts a merge while performing a cherry-pick; the bases differ. On the current set the two agree everywhere, so this is a latent divergence rather than a live defect [measured] -- fix it while the code is open.

  D. Clear state["conflicts"][uid] on EVERY retirement path, not only in the re-test loop.

  E. After a successful cherry-pick, run the gate on the files it touched. `touched` is already computed at line 872. Run: `ruff check <touched>`, `python -m mypy --config-file mypy.ini <touched>`, and `python .github/scripts/check_merge_acceptance.py --files <touched>`. On any failure, REVERT (git reset --hard to the pre-merge sha) and re-escalate with the tool output in the conflict message. Scope the gate to touched files, not the whole tree, so a pre-existing red file does not block unrelated merges.

  F. Change the escalation banner to print retirements as their own count: 'driver: ESCALATION -- 5 escalated, 2 retired without review'. The count the principal sees must GROW when the classifier gets busier, not shrink; a banner that quietens as more code lands unexamined is an instrument wired backwards.

WHAT MUST NOT BE DONE. mypy MUST be invoked as `--config-file mypy.ini`, never bare `--strict`: warn_unreachable lives in the ini, and on the T01 specimen `mypy --strict` from a scratch directory reports 'Success: no issues found' while the same file under mypy.ini reports 'Statement is unreachable' [measured]. Do NOT lower the 99% coverage bar or the 20-line minimum to retire more units. Do NOT enable rerere in this unit. Do NOT add any resolver, union driver or .gitattributes merge= line.

(2) A new test asserts no uid appears in both state["conflicts"] and state["force_done"] -- run against the live state file today this FAILS on K01, which is the regression it locks shut. BN.title: rebase unmerged worktrees every tick and serialise units that design the same subsystem
BN.commit: feat(driver): keep worktrees current and refuse concurrent duplicate-subsystem units
BN.note:
MERGE RESILIENCE. Specified by the merge-resolution workflow on 24 August 2026 after reading the code and measuring against the live tree. Every claim in this brief was measured.

THE DEFECT. The driver creates the conflicts it then struggles to resolve, by two mechanisms, both measured.

  (1) rebase_worktree is defined at .harness/build_driver.py:514 and called from EXACTLY ONE place -- line 918, inside the conflict branch of merge_unit_worktree, and only when the unit is quiescent [measured: grep]. A worktree is therefore never rebased before its build, nor on any tick while it sits finished and unmerged. N03 wrote its commit at 16:43 on 24 August against a base from 19:40 on 23 August: 160 commits and 21 hours behind [measured]. It was asked to write a patch against a repository that no longer exists.

  (2) Two units designing the same subsystem collide by construction. coordination.py produced 7 of today's 42 conflict hunks because N03 ('short fencing-token leases replacing the one-hour claim') and T02 ('atomic readiness, claim and fencing') both designed the dispatch lease. Together with AI -- a second design of build_driver.py itself, 22 hunks -- those units account for 28 of 42 hunks, 67% of all conflict volume [measured].

WHAT PREDICTS A CONFLICT HERE, and what does not [measured 24 Aug 2026]. Pearson r between 'commits that landed to the files this unit touched since its branch base' and hunk count is 0.81 (n=7). Pearson r between drift in HOURS and hunk count is -0.08. So it is co-churn, not staleness. And claim count predicts nothing: src/consilient/events.py is claimed by 39 units and produced ZERO hunks, while .harness/build_driver.py is claimed by 6 and produced 22. Do not narrow claims to fix conflicts -- it would not have prevented one of today's seven.

WHAT TO BUILD.

  A. Rebase every unmerged, quiescent worktree onto HEAD each tick, not only after a conflict. Reuse rebase_worktree unchanged; move the call site so it runs over the same `mergeable` set the merge loop already computes, BEFORE attempting the merge. Preserve the existing quiescence test exactly -- rebasing under a live dispatcher rewrites the branch beneath the worker, and the docstring at line 525 says so. Log each rebase with the number of commits it replayed, so the effect is visible.

  B. In ready() at line 1235, refuse to make two units concurrently startable when their titles name the same subsystem AND they share a claimed path. Concretely: stop-word the tokens of `title + ' ' + commit`, take the Jaccard of the two token sets, and if it exceeds the threshold while the pair shares at least one claimed path and the other unit is in flight, the second is not startable -- it waits. Serialise, do not warn. Measured on the current plan: 8,646 unit pairs, 1,906 of which share at least one claimed path; N03/T02 ranks 10 of 1,906 (0.52%) on {claim, coordination, fencing} with two shared claims, and both are escalated right now. K01 appears in three of the top sixteen pairs (K01/K02 #4, AX/K01 #8, AR/K01 #16) and is also escalated. A top-20 cut fires on 1.0% of claim-sharing pairs and 0.23% of all pairs.

WHAT MUST NOT BE DONE. Do NOT make the threshold a warning, a print, or an advisory field: ConE issued 775 notifications over 26,000 pull requests -- 3% -- and its authors rejected the academic prediction literature outright because precision of 0.48-0.63 produces too many false alarms to survive [cited]. A warning that fires on every unit touching a hot file would be ignored by the second tick. Do NOT cap or narrow declared claims as a conflict remedy -- refuted above; it is a throughput fix, not a conflict fix, and belongs in its own unit if wanted. Do NOT rebase a worktree whose dispatcher is alive. Do NOT hard-code the threshold with no way to change it: it is a knob and the physical world needs tuning.

DONE WHEN. (1) A test asserts ready() refuses to make N03 and T02 concurrently startable given the real plan-units.json, and permits them when serialised. (2) A test asserts the firing rate over all 1,906 claim-sharing pairs is <= 5%; if a future plan pushes it above that, the threshold is wrong and must be TIGHTENED, never tolerated. (3) A test asserts rebase is not attempted for a unit with a live dispatcher. (4) Every firing is logged, so the rate can be reviewed weekly against ConE's 3%.

BO.title: record every merge event with its class so merge beta can be measured later
BO.commit: feat(driver): record merge events as evidence for a later beta measurement
BO.note:
MERGE RESILIENCE. Specified by the merge-resolution workflow on 24 August 2026 after reading the code and measuring against the live tree. Every claim in this brief was measured.

THE DEFECT. This project measures beta -- the rate at which an automated check accepts a bad artefact -- and a merge gate is a check, so it has one. Nothing records the merge events it would be computed from, and no published tool or benchmark reports this number: Mergiraf/MergirafSemi, JDime, FSTMerge, jFSTMerge, S3M, Spork, IntelliMerge, AutoMerge, DeepMerge, MergeBERT, MergeGen, SBCR, Merge-Bench, ConflictBench and ConGra were all searched; the closest proxies measure 'conflict not reported', not 'resolution wrong', and Merge-Bench states outright that it approximates correctness with source-code equivalence [cited]. State that as 'we searched these and found none', NEVER as a superlative.

WHAT TO BUILD. Recording only. Append one JSON line per merge event to .harness/merge-events.jsonl (untracked; it is instance data): timestamp, uid, worktree head sha, resulting HEAD sha, the class -- one of clean_cherry_pick, classifier_retirement, gated_merge, escalated -- which classifier rung produced any retirement verdict, the touched file list, the gate's verdict and its per-check output, and, for a retirement, the coverage percentage and the sha it was retired against. Where a unit was built more than once, name the DISCARDED sha and the count of test functions in it that appear in no file in HEAD: 33% of conflicted units carry the double-build signature and Y01's discarded build took four refusal tests with it, unremarked [cited, Evidence 2]. Silent loss of test coverage is precisely what beta exists to notice.

WHAT MUST NOT BE DONE. Do NOT compute, print, render or publish a beta figure in this unit. MIN_REJECTIONS = 30: fewer than 30 principal-authored rejections and the only honest output is insufficient_data, because an underpowered beta is worse than none -- it is quotable. Do NOT let a model author a verdict (V0-18): a model adjudicating a model's merge is echo arriving through the data layer, and the 2026 calibrated-judge paper's own judge accepted 4 of the 5 structurally invalid resolutions it was asked to catch [cited]. Do NOT multiply the per-check rates: EXP-47 measured joint survival at 33.82% against 26.86% predicted by independence, odds ratio 5.15 [cited, repository] -- per-check rates are diagnostics and the composite is the only routing input. Do NOT sample only gate-accepted merges: conditioning on the gate's own verdict makes beta 1 by construction. Do NOT record the whole population as one number: today it is 5 gated events against 72 clean landings, roughly 6% of merge traffic, so a figure from the gated stratum would be quoted as the system's false-accept rate. Stratify into clean_cherry_pick, classifier_retirement and gated_merge, and name the stratum every time the number is quoted.

AND SAY WHAT IS STILL UNRESOLVED, in the code comment as well as the record. Two things this design does not settle: (i) how to afford 30 adjudications in the CLEAN stratum, which is 94% of traffic and completely unobserved; (ii) whether adjudication by reading is a different class of facts at all -- it is not, since a 313-line verbatim duplicate in src/consilient/harness.py survived every human glance it ever got. The adjudication question must be behavioural ('the merged tree answers X; HEAD before answered Y; which is correct?'), which is executed output and answerable in five seconds.

DONE WHEN. (1) One driver tick appends a well-formed line per merge event, and a test asserts every line carries a stratum, a provenance rung and a resulting sha. (2) A test asserts the recorder refuses to emit any rate, ratio or percentage -- it records events, it does not compute beta. (3) A test asserts a unit built more than once records its discarded sha and that sha's count of HEAD-absent test functions.

Z02.title: bound the driver's counters and stop counting other people's processes
Z02.commit: driver: un-refundable restart intensity, review cap, quarantine, own-state liveness
Z02.note:
FOUR DEFECTS IN ONE FILE, all measured in .harness/driver-state.json on 24 Aug 2026.

(1) THE REVIEW PATH IS UNCAPPED. state['review_attempts'][uid] is incremented and compared to a ceiling NOWHERE. Live: 67 units, max 27 attempts on one, rising within a single sitting. The adversarial review path is the second class of facts -- it is the product -- and it is the only dispatch path with no supervision.

(3) NO QUARANTINE. The 3-identical-deaths branch prints and continues; reclamation pops and refunds next tick, so nothing is ever terminal. `grep quarantined` finds nothing in the driver.

(b) Add `total_restarts`, a list of restart timestamps that NO path may decrement; discard entries older than 10 minutes; when more than 6 remain, stop dispatching, set `quarantined`, escalate once. Keep the refundable `attempts` counter unchanged -- the refund is right about evidence and wrong about load, so this is a SECOND counter, not a replacement. (c) Make `quarantined` a real state reclamation does not clear; cleared only by a landed check or an explicit human decision. (d) Derive live_dispatchers() from this driver's own state['in_flight'].

MUST NOT. Do not classify failures before counting them -- OTP counts restarts precisely because classification is where the mistake is made. Do not add any new refund path. Do not lower the existing attempt cap, and do not raise it to make anything pass. Do not keep a process-command-line match as a fallback.

DONE WHEN. Tests assert total_restarts is monotonic across every state transition and no path decrements it; crossing the window sets quarantined; review_attempts past 3 refuses; live_dispatchers ignores an unrelated dispatch.py process. Full suite green.

Z03.title: checkpoint the driver tick and bound every subprocess
Z03.commit: loop: checkpoint per phase, require explicit timeouts, kill the process tree
Z03.note:
METASTABLE FAILURE. Cited: Bronson, Aghayev, Charapko, Zhu, 'Metastable Failures in Distributed Systems', HotOS '21, pp. 221-227, DOI 10.1145/3458336.3465286; Huang et al., 'Metastable Failures in the Wild', OSDI '22, pp. 73-90.

COMPONENT. build_loop.py calls subprocess.run(build_driver.py, timeout=3000). Inside a tick, suite_green() calls sh([python, -m, pytest, ...]) and sh() has NO timeout parameter and no default. save_state() is called at exactly three terminal places. THEREFORE a tick killed at the deadline persists NOTHING: consumed review receipts, reclaimed slots, cleared conflicts and attempt refunds all vanish and the next tick redoes the work.

AMPLIFICATION, already measured in this repo: two concurrent drivers put nine pytest processes on the box and the suite went 432 s -> 961 s, a capacity degradation factor of about 2.2 at n=9. And per this machine's own recorded lesson, a subprocess timeout does not kill grandchildren, so an orphaned pytest outlives the tick that spawned it and contends with the next tick's. Once suite duration exceeds the deadline, every tick is killed before it can persist progress, each abandoned tick leaves another orphan, goodput is zero, and removing the original cause does not recover it -- which is the definition of metastable. NOT YET HIT: the suite currently runs ~291 s against a 3000 s deadline, a margin of about 10x, shrinking with the test count.

FIX. (1) save_state after every state-mutating phase, not only at exit, so a killed tick keeps what it earned. (2) Make sh() require an explicit timeout with no default, so an unbounded subprocess is a type error rather than a habit. (3) Kill the process tree on timeout using the existing scripts/proc_tree.py helper. (4) A test asserting suite_green is invoked at most once per tick and behind a bounded deadline.

EXPERIMENT that would refute the exposure: inject a long sleep into one test, run the loop, and assert the tick is killed, driver-state.json mtime is unchanged, and a pytest process outlives the tick. Refuted if the tick checkpoints.

MUST NOT. Do not raise the 3000 s deadline to buy margin -- that widens the window without removing the amplification. Do not disable suite_green.

Z04.title: untrack mutable harness state and the nested source copies
Z04.commit: harness: untrack mutable driver state, locks and nested source copies
Z04.note:
DEFECT. The files that decide what the driver dispatches are tracked git objects in the tree the agents edit, so any `git checkout` can restore an older copy. This has already happened once: .harness/plan-units.json silently lost a queued unit to a checkout and nobody noticed.

MEASURED 24 Aug 2026: `git ls-files .harness` returns driver-state.json (the authoritative scheduling record, ~720 KB), plan-units.json, driver-tick.lock (a LOCK FILE in version control), build-loop.out, build-loop.err, and two complete extra copies of src/consilient/ under .harness/exp-*/ and .harness/s02-mut-*/ -- so `git ls-files` returns three consilient/events.py. The nested copies also make module='src/consilient/events.py' ambiguous for the guard-mutation registry. Note .harness/log/ is already gitignored and has never suffered this.

FIX. `git rm -r --cached` those paths -- INDEX ONLY, do NOT delete any file from disk, the driver is writing driver-state.json continuously. Add matching .gitignore entries. Add a test that runs `git ls-files .harness` and fails if it returns driver-state.json, plan-units.json, any *.lock, build-loop.*, or any path matching .harness/**/src/consilient/.

MUST NOT. Do not delete files from disk. Do not touch .harness/log/. Do not add a blanket .harness/ ignore -- HANDOFF.md, build_driver.py, build_loop.py, board_snapshot.py and the example configs are legitimately tracked and must stay tracked.

DONE WHEN. `git ls-files .harness` returns only source and documentation; the new test fails when any untracked path is re-added (verify by staging one); full suite green.

Z05.title: put full jitter on every retry backoff
Z05.commit: fix(events): jitter every retry backoff, which was putting twenty readers on one instant
Z05.note:
ALREADY IMPLEMENTED by the orchestrator on 24 August 2026, by hand, because this defect was blocking the queue that would otherwise have built it. It still needs an adversarial review from a different model family -- work checked only by whoever did it is the echo failure this project exists to detect, and that applies to the orchestrator exactly as it applies to any dispatched agent.

REVIEW THIS, DO NOT REBUILD IT. Read the commit named above and attack it.

RETRY STORM / THUNDERING HERD. Cited: Marc Brooker, 'Exponential Backoff And Jitter', AWS Architecture Blog, 4 March 2015, which carries the simulator and the comparison of no-backoff / exponential / full / equal / decorrelated jitter. Google SRE Book ch. 22, 'Addressing Cascading Failures', is the standard operational treatment.

COMPONENT. src/consilient/events.py (_READ_RETRIES = 6, _READ_BACKOFF = 0.04, time.sleep(_READ_BACKOFF * (2**attempt))) and src/consilient/cli.py::cmd_doctor (time.sleep(_DB_BUSY_BACKOFF * (2**attempt))). Both are exponential backoff with ZERO jitter, on resources this repo's own comments describe as contended by ~20 concurrent agents: the append-only trajectory JSONL, where Windows denies a reader while a writer holds the file, and the SQLite state database. Twenty readers evicted by one writer all sleep 40 ms, then 80, then 160, in lockstep.

WHY IT ESCALATES. The ~2.5 s budget then fails closed, and the code comment records the cost: it 'failed the suite -- which then blocked retirement, merging and publication at once'. A synchronised herd on one file escalates to a global goodput stop. The PermissionError outage has already happened here; the herd form has not.

FIX. One shared helper `events._retry_sleep(attempt)` implementing full jitter -- sleep(random.uniform(0, base * 2**attempt)) -- used by EVERY retry site, plus a test that fails on any time.sleep() whose argument contains '2**'.

MUST NOT. Raising _READ_RETRIES or lengthening the budget is explicitly NOT the remedy: it widens the window without decorrelating anything. Note Z01 removes most of the offered load on this path; this unit removes the synchronisation, and both are wanted.

EXPERIMENT. 20 processes each appending 200 events while a 21st reads in a loop; record the distribution of attempt counts and terminal failures with and without jitter at identical offered load. Exposure confirmed if the failure rate drops materially under jitter.

Z06.title: bulkhead the build and review lanes
Z06.commit: driver: separate admission pools so one lane cannot starve the other
Z06.note:
CASCADING FAILURE / NO BULKHEAD. Cited: Huang et al., HotOS '17 section 2.3, which traces one end to end -- a mis-detected capacity fault leads to repeated reroute-crash-reboot, servers removed from service, pressure on survivors, 'and naturally, this eventually led to a catastrophic cascading failure'. Standard operational treatments: Google SRE Book ch. 22; Nygard, Release It! (bulkheads, circuit breakers).

COMPONENT. build_driver.py, MAX_CONCURRENT = MAX_BUILDS + MAX_REVIEWS (24 + 12 = 36) -- a SINGLE pool, with admission written as `reviews_out >= MAX_REVIEWS or live >= MAX_CONCURRENT` and `launched >= MAX_BUILDS or live + launched >= MAX_CONCURRENT`. There is no bulkhead between the lanes: a review backlog consumes slots builds need, and vice versa. This was observed live -- 64 reviews in flight while builds could not start.

FIX. Two independent pools with their own admission, so neither lane can consume the other's capacity, and a lane at its ceiling sheds rather than borrowing.

MUST NOT. Do not raise MAX_CONCURRENT to paper over contention -- the machine's measured degradation factor at n=9 pytest processes is about 2.2, so more concurrency makes the suite slower, which is the amplification loop Z03 addresses. Note MAX_CONCURRENT is currently doing load-shedding work nobody assigned it, documented only as 'a load cap on the machine'; a safety property held by an incidental constant is itself the finding, so make the shedding explicit and tested.

Z07.title: make the recall pack carry something, or admit it carries nothing
Z07.commit: recall: select summaries so a pack is not empty at the character limit
Z07.note:
MEASURED 25 August 2026, found while fixing the scan cost that had stopped dispatch entirely.

THE RECALL PACK IS EMPTY. `instructions.assemble` against the live trajectory returns a selection with ZERO selected events and 201 omissions, and a pack of 160 bytes whose entire content is the apology:

  _Context incomplete: 201 event(s) omitted to fit character limit of 8000._

It is not a regression from the scan bound: Z01's original evidence already recorded `data.recall.selected_event_ids` as EMPTY in a sampled event, back when the same event carried an 84,603-byte omitted list. The recall layer has been contributing NOTHING to briefs for some time, while costing more every day.

CAUSE. RECALL_LIMIT_CHARS is 8,000 and the events competing for it are far larger than that individually. Measured over the current candidate set:

  dispatch.outcome   845 events   6,778,908 chars  (about 8 KB each)
  capability.gap     578 events   4,657,831 chars  (about 8 KB each)
  dispatch.refused   118 events   1,333,841 chars

A single dispatch.outcome fills the whole budget, so the shrink-to-receipt loop drops everything and returns nothing. The selection is all-or-nothing per event, and no event fits.

FIX, and the shape matters. Do NOT simply raise RECALL_LIMIT_CHARS -- that widens the budget without making selection discriminating, and it puts 8 KB of one dispatch outcome into a brief that needed a sentence. Select a SUMMARY projection of an event when its full form does not fit: for dispatch.outcome that is the unit, harness, status and reason; for capability.gap the capability and the gap. The receipt must record that a summary was selected rather than the full event, so a replay can tell the two apart and the digest still discriminates.

MUST NOT. Do not raise the character limit to make a pack non-empty. Do not drop the omission accounting. Do not weaken `_guard_privileged_selection` -- a summary must still be refused if it carries a privileged field. Do not change RECALL_SCAN_EVENTS or PROTECTED_SCAN_EVENTS; those bound the SCAN and are a separate concern already fixed.

DONE WHEN. (1) Against the repository's own trajectory, assemble returns a pack with at least one selected item and a non-trivial body. (2) A test pins that an event larger than the character limit is represented by a summary rather than dropped. (3) `instructions.verify` still matches on replay, for an event recorded before this change and one after. (4) A test fails if the pack is empty while events were available -- an empty pack must be a reported outcome, never the silent default. (5) Full suite green.

Z09.title: measure beta against upstream maintainers, submission decoupled from the verifier
Z09.commit: beta: admit upstream maintainer verdicts under a declared admission bar
Z09.note:
JOE, 25 August 2026, second formulation and it is the one that works: submit the PR BEFORE the verifiers run, then measure where the verifier accepted and the PR was eventually rejected.

WHY THIS IS THE RIGHT SHAPE. The defect in the first formulation was that submitting only what our checks passed conditions the sample on the verifier's own outcome, so every rejected row carries verifier_accept=True and beta is 1 by construction -- beta.py names that failure exactly, and the rendered output prints 'NOT a bound: sampling not declared unconditioned on the verifier'. Deciding to submit BEFORE the verifier runs removes the dependence at its source. It also measures OUR OWN task family, which Z10 cannot.

TAKEN LITERALLY IT BREAKS TWICE, and the second break is worse than the first.

  1. Submitting genuinely unchecked work to volunteer maintainers spends their time on      code we knowingly had not verified, in the communities this project is trying to      contribute to.
  2. UPSTREAM CI CONTAMINATES THE ORACLE. Most projects run tests on every PR. A broken      submission is then rejected by THEIR automated checks, not by a human judging      correctness -- so the 'human rejection' is often another automated verifier wearing      a human's clothes, which is precisely what beta must not be measured against.

THE DESIGN THAT KEEPS THE INSIGHT. Decouple submission from THE VERIFIER BEING MEASURED, not from all checking. Gate submission on a pre-declared MINIMAL ADMISSION BAR that is explicitly not the composite verifier: it builds, the project's existing suite passes, and the contribution is one that project actually wants. Then run the composite verifier and record its verdict SEPARATELY, without it influencing whether we submit.

Within the admitted population the composite verifier's verdict is free to vary, so both cells exist -- composite-accepted / maintainer-rejected AND composite-rejected / maintainer-merged -- and nothing obviously broken is ever sent. The estimand is then honestly 'beta conditional on passing the admission bar', which is a declarable sampling protocol rather than a silent truncation.

THE SELF-CHECK THAT DECIDES WHETHER THIS WORKED, and it must be reported whether or not it is flattering: what fraction of ADMITTED artefacts does the composite verifier reject? If the admission bar is nearly as strong as the composite verifier, that fraction approaches zero, the variation collapses and we are back to beta = 1 by a slower route. Report the fraction with every figure. If it is under a pre-registered floor, the protocol has failed and the honest output is insufficient_data, not a number.

SEPARATE THE TWO REJECTERS IN THE RECORD. Store the upstream CI outcome and the human decision as different fields. A PR closed because their CI went red is NOT a human correctness verdict and must not enter the numerator. Only a maintainer's judgement that the change is wrong counts; scope, roadmap, staleness and house style are rejections of FIT and are excluded too. Record the maintainer's own words verbatim, and do not let the agent that wrote the PR classify its own rejection.

AUTHENTICATION IS AN OPEN GOVERNANCE QUESTION AND IS THE PRINCIPAL'S. `admits_human_beta_row` requires estimand_kind == HUMAN_VERDICT_BETA and auth_status == 'authenticated', and V0-18 has meant verdicts authored by the PRINCIPAL. Whether a third-party maintainer's decision counts as an authenticated human verdict for the GATE quantity is an ADR, not this unit's call. Until that ADR exists, record these rows under a proxy estimand kind so they cannot reach the gate, and build the collection so the kind can be switched by a one-line change if the principal accepts it.

MUST NOT. Never submit a contribution that is not wanted on its own merits, and never weaken one to see whether the verifier catches it -- a deliberately weak PR is not drawn from the distribution the harness produces, so its rejection measures nothing. Do not count a CI failure as a human verdict. Do not set lower_bound_on_joint_error until the admission bar and its rejection fraction are recorded in the register. Do not lower MIN_REJECTIONS to make a figure reportable.

DONE WHEN. (1) The admission bar is pre-registered in the experiment register, at the next free EXP number after EXP-143, with its scope, stopping rule, classification rule, abuse prohibition and the rejection-fraction floor below which the protocol is declared failed. (2) The schema records composite-verifier verdict, upstream CI outcome and human decision as three separate fields, with a test that a CI failure alone cannot enter the numerator. (3) A test asserts BOTH cells are representable, because a schema that can only express one recreates the conditioning in the data model. (4) The verifier verdict is timestamped and a test refuses any row whose verdict postdates the submission, since the whole property is that the verdict did not gate the submission. (5) Rows are recorded under a proxy estimand kind and a test asserts they are excluded from the gate quantity until an ADR says otherwise. (6) Full suite green.

Z10.title: measure a real beta by judging upstream PRs we did not write
Z10.commit: exp: measure beta against upstream maintainer verdicts on PRs we did not write
Z10.note:
THE UNCONDITIONED HALF OF Z09, and the reason it matters is that Z09 cannot be a real beta while Z10 can.

Z09 has us submit PRs and count maintainer rejections. Its sample is conditioned on our own verifier -- we submit only what our checks passed -- so every rejected row carries verifier_accept=True and beta is 1 by construction. beta.py names that exact failure. Z09 is therefore a lower bound on the numerator and nothing more.

INVERT THE ROLES AND THE CONDITIONING DISAPPEARS. Take PRs OTHER people submitted to the upstream repositories we already track. Run our composite verifier over each one and record its accept/reject BEFORE the maintainer decides. Then record what the maintainer actually did. The maintainer has never seen our checks and their decision cannot depend on them, so the sample is not conditioned on the verifier's own outcome -- which is precisely the property `lower_bound_on_joint_error` requires and which Z09 cannot have. Both cells of the table are observable: artefacts our checks accepted that the maintainer rejected, AND artefacts our checks rejected that the maintainer merged.

That second cell is the one this project has never seen. It is also the cheaper measure in every sense: no volunteer maintainer's time is spent, nothing is submitted, and the sample size is bounded by upstream's PR traffic rather than by our own output rate.

RECORD THE PREDICTION BEFORE THE OUTCOME. If our verdict is computed after the merge is visible it is not a prediction, and nothing in the record would show the difference. Stamp our verdict with the commit it judged and the time, and refuse any row whose verdict timestamp is later than the maintainer's decision.

TASK FAMILY, STATED HONESTLY. This measures beta for 'PRs submitted to project X by third parties', which is NOT the family our own harness produces. The skill forbids comparing beta figures across different check sets or families, so this figure may not be quoted as the harness's own beta, and the register entry must say which family it describes. It is still the first unconditioned human-verdict beta available to this project, and it calibrates the verifier against real human judgement, which is the thing the gate quantity is supposed to be about.

MUST NOT. Do not interact with the upstream PR in any way -- no comment, no review, no approval -- because influencing the maintainer's decision reintroduces the dependence this design exists to remove. Do not count a PR closed for scope, staleness or inactivity; only a decision about whether the change is CORRECT is a verdict. Do not set `lower_bound_on_joint_error` without showing the protocol in the register. Do not lower MIN_REJECTIONS.

DONE WHEN. (1) A pre-registered protocol in the experiment register naming the repositories, the sampling frame, the stopping rule and the task family, at the next free EXP number. (2) A collector that records our verdict with its timestamp and the judged commit, refusing any row whose verdict postdates the maintainer's decision, with a test for that refusal. (3) A test asserting BOTH cells are representable -- checks-accepted / human-rejected and checks-rejected / human-accepted -- because a schema that can only express one of them recreates the conditioning in the data model. (4) Full suite green.

Z11.title: upstream contribution as a standing capability, with outcomes recorded
Z11.commit: feat(upstream): contribute to external repositories and record every outcome
Z11.note:
JOE, 25 August 2026: "We should automate upstream contributions to other open source repos in line with our own development and learn from those that are merged, those that are rejected, any comments or engagement... This should be a systematic feature of Consilient."

BUILD THE CAPABILITY. Consilient identifies work it is doing anyway that belongs upstream, prepares it against the host project's contribution rules, runs THEIR CI to green, submits it, and then records every outcome: merged, rejected, revised-then-merged, closed without a decision, and every review comment. That record is a standing asset -- it serves Gate B4's twenty non-Consilient tickets, it is genuinely different-class supervision for learning, and it is the only human oracle available that does not route through the principal.

NAME THE QUANTITY CORRECTLY, because this is where it would go wrong. If a PR is submitted ONLY when our verifier accepted it, then what the merge/reject outcome measures is

    P(a maintainer rejects | our verifier accepted)

which is the FALSE-ACCEPT RATE AMONG ACCEPTED WORK. That is a real, useful and directly actionable number, and this unit should compute and report it. It is NOT beta.

Beta is P(our verifier accepts | the artefact is bad). Estimating it needs the other cell -- artefacts a human judged bad that our verifier REJECTED -- and those never get submitted, so they are unobservable through this channel. Every rejected row would carry verifier_accept=True and the ratio would be 1 by construction, which beta.py names in its module docstring and which the rendered output flags as 'NOT a bound: sampling not declared unconditioned on the verifier'. Reporting this number AS beta would be the exact failure this project exists to detect, committed by us, in our own headline metric.

So: report it under its own name, with its own field, and make it impossible to read as beta. Z09 holds the design that does yield beta (submission gated on an admission bar that is not our verifier, so both cells vary); Z10 holds the inverted cross-check. This unit is the capability and the false-accept rate; it is not the beta route.

LEARNING SIGNAL. Merged, rejected, revised-then-merged and the review comments are supervision from outside our own model and prompt -- a genuinely different class of facts, which is the whole test in CONSILIENCE.md. Record it, and record refusals and non-response too, since a PR nobody looked at is not evidence of quality.

MUST NOT. Never open a PR that is not a contribution the project would want on its own merits, and never weaken one to see whether it is caught. Never argue a maintainer toward an outcome -- influencing the verdict makes it ours wearing their name. Respect each project's contribution policy, including any that prohibit or require disclosure of automated submissions, and disclose that the change was machine-authored wherever the project asks or where a reasonable maintainer would want to know. Harvested outcomes are instance data under ADR-0057 and are never published from this repository. Do not report the resulting rate as beta, and do not add it to the gate quantity.

DONE WHEN. (1) The capability can prepare, CI-verify and submit a change to a named external repository, and refuses to submit when the project's CI is not green. (2) Every outcome class is recorded, including non-response, with the maintainer's words verbatim. (3) The false-accept-among-accepted rate is computed and reported under a name that is not beta, with a test asserting it cannot enter the human-beta projection or the gate. (4) A test asserts a submission is refused when the project's policy prohibits automated PRs. (5) Harvested outcomes are untracked instance data, with a test. (6) Full suite green.
